root_cause.text: KVM’s nested SVM VMLOAD/VMSAVE emulation used `svm->vmcb` (the current VMCB, i.e. vmcb02 in nested guests) instead of always using `vmcb01`, causing L2 VMLOAD/VMSAVE state to be copied to or from the wrong VMCB.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `svm_copy_vmloadsave_state(svm->vmcb, vmcb12)` to `svm_copy_vmloadsave_state(svm->vmcb01.ptr, vmcb12)` and the reverse direction likewise, with the added comment “KVM always performs VMLOAD/VMSAVE on VMCB01,” and the CVE text states the bug occurs when L2 executes VMSAVE/VMLOAD not intercepted by L1 and KVM “will mistakenly use vmcb02.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: KVM’s nested SVM VMLOAD/VMSAVE emulation used `svm->vmcb` (the current VMCB, i.e. vmcb02 in nested guests) instead of always using `vmcb01`, causing L2 VMLOAD/VMSAVE state to be copied to or from the wrong VMCB.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `svm_copy_vmloadsave_state(svm->vmcb, vmcb12)` to `svm_copy_vmloadsave_state(svm->vmcb01.ptr, vmcb12)` and the reverse direction likewise, with the added comment “KVM always performs VMLOAD/VMSAVE on VMCB01,” and the CVE text states the bug occurs when L2 executes VMSAVE/VMLOAD not intercepted by L1 and KVM “will mistakenly use vmcb02.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix VMLOAD/VMSAVE interception to operate on VMCB01, matching the actual KVM run path.
intent_record.what: The VMLOAD/VMSAVE interception handler was changed to use `svm->vmcb01.ptr` instead of `svm->vmcb` when calling `svm_copy_vmloadsave_state()`, and a comment was added noting that KVM always performs VMLOAD/VMSAVE on VMCB01 in `__svm_vcpu_run()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, VMLOAD/VMSAVE state is now copied to and from the active VMCB01 structure rather than the generic `svm->vmcb` pointer, aligning the interception handling with the execution path actually used by KVM and preventing state from being written to or read from the wrong control block.

grouping_result.intent: Fix VMLOAD/VMSAVE interception to operate on VMCB01, matching the actual KVM run path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: nested SVM VMLOAD/VMSAVE was using the current VMCB instead of vmcb01, and this group fixes the interception to operate on VMCB01.

candidates.rationale: This line copies VMLOAD state from the current VMCB pointer `svm->vmcb`, which in nested operation can be vmcb02 instead of the required vmcb01, causing L2 VMLOAD state to be written to the wrong VMCB.
This line copies VMSAVE state into `svm->vmcb`, again using the current VMCB rather than always vmcb01, so nested guest state can be read from or saved to the wrong VMCB.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement copies VMLOAD state from `svm->vmcb`, which in nested SVM can point to vmcb02 instead of vmcb01, so L2 VMLOAD state is taken from the wrong VMCB.
This statement saves VMSAVE state into `svm->vmcb`, which in nested SVM can be vmcb02 instead of vmcb01, so L2 VMSAVE state is written to or read from the wrong VMCB.
